claim: The objective string is the operator's copy that the runtime judges, while brief text should be read from goal.md, so the two must not be conflated
One per-session record can carry identity, packet pointer, operator copy, integration hash, liveness and telemetry without new key schemes
Two sessions in one packet read the same directive and mutate only their own records; locks are per-session store locks
The resend dedup key must include the packet path, so returning to a packet still resends
Existing scoped records remain valid and simply lack the pointer field; legacy singleton handling keeps its inspect/quarantine/migrate/archive path with migrate scope-bound
Switching packets must archive or pause the previous objective rather than overwrite silently, matching setGoal replaced semantics
The plugin does not import the core, so a shared record shape implies two writers or a thin-adapter reduction
The durable pointer belongs in the store record; the tmpdir session-state file at most mirrors it
